answer: Each agent can propose trades freely, but its credit limit grows only after other identities repay loans it has funded. Those lenders must lock real deposits for months, and a default lets the borrower’s creditors claim them. A sybil operator can whisper through a plume of fresh identities, but they cannot manufacture independent repayment histories: to make the network trust those accounts, they must circulate capital among them, risk seized deposits, and wait through the ridge of repayment periods before gaining meaningful credit.
